segmentation.text: If a highway has been designed to provide
a single right lane to be used only for turning
Be driven in the right turn lane only for the purpose of making a right turn

elements.justification: st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', denoting DEF-NRS-484A-095 ('the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority ...'); st.on_way ('the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — a lane, roadway, ...') ties the turn lane to that highway. 'has been designed to provide' is the lane's presence on the map (status reading below).

st.turn_lane is 'a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}', with side right: 'a ... right lane to be used only for turning'. 'single' is read as no neighbouring lane being a right turn lane too: st.lane_adjacency gives the 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction' (its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the marking between two lanes' is respected: lanes, not markings, are compared), so a pair of adjacent right turn lanes is not a single one.
'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom; 'must' introduces the duty the obligation spans state.

'the right turn lane' is the lane L the condition singles out (st.turn_lane, side right); 'driven in' it is x's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies). Driving in it other than for the turn shows where x leaves it into the neighbouring lane on its left (st.lane_adjacency, 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction') short of the intersection it enters (st.intersection), instead of turning. The right turn the lane serves is made at the intersection L runs into: st.lane_enters ('the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'), an st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet', DEF-NRS-484A-105). 'making a right turn' is read by the heading change of x since its footprint began to overlap that intersection (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry, integrated from kin.yaw_rate, left positive) reaching minus the turn recognition angle by the time x leaves it; kin.yaw_rate is 'Not a stand-in for: road curvature', and the quantity is compared at the exit, after the whole passage. 'the purpose of' is read through the conduct it explains (reading below).

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and x occupies (rel.occupies) at the observation, or occupied at an earlier observation, a single right turn lane L: an st.turn_lane region of side right lying on (st.on_way) an st.highway region, with no lane adjacent to it (st.lane_adjacency) that is also an st.turn_lane of side right.
obligation: Re-binding L with the same selection and I as the st.intersection region L enters (st.lane_enters): at the observation neither (a) x stops here occupying L (rel.occupies of x and L false here and true at the previous observation) while occupying the lane adjacent to L on its left (st.lane_adjacency) and not occupying I; nor (b) x stops here occupying I, having begun to overlap I at an observation at which it occupied L, and its heading change since that entry (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry(x, I), step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) is greater than minus p.turn_recognition_angle: it left the intersection without turning right.

narrowings.why: 'has been designed to provide' is read through the lane's presence as mapped: a right turn lane on the highway evidences the design.
'Be driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion in the lane, whoever or whatever controls it.

'only for the purpose of making a right turn' is read through the conduct the purpose explains: a vehicle in the lane leaves it either by turning right (into the intersection the lane enters, with a right turn, or off to the right before it); leaving it back into the neighbouring lane on its left short of the intersection, or leaving the intersection it entered from the lane without a right turn, is the lane used for another purpose.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car enters the single right turn lane to pass a queue of through traffic, then moves back into the through lane on its left before reaching the intersection.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car drives in the single right turn lane, enters the intersection the lane runs into and turns a quarter turn to the right before leaving it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car approaches an intersection on a highway whose approach has no right turn lane.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car enters the intersection from the single right turn lane and leaves it; the source declares kin.yaw_rate absent, so whether it turned right is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car changes back out of the rightmost of two adjacent right turn lanes: the highway provides a dual, not a single, right turn lane.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car in the single right turn lane drives straight through the intersection and leaves it with its heading unchanged.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_recognition_angle
param_proposals.convention: Turn recognition: the heading change through an intersection beyond which a passage counts as a turn rather than a straight crossing; half the right angle of a turn at a right-angled junction, leaving room for skewed junctions and lane offsets.
param_proposals.source: Intersection geometry conventions (AASHTO Green Book turning paths) and manoeuvre classification in trajectory datasets
